title: Lupin Posts 16% Profit Growth in Q1 FY27 as Revenue Tops Rs 8,200 Crore
excerpt: The Indian pharma major beat analyst expectations with expanding margins, though competition on key U.S. products looms over the remainder of the fiscal year.
body:
• Lupin reported Q1 FY27 consolidated net profit of approximately Rs 1,415 crore, up 16% year-on-year
  • Revenue from operations exceeded Rs 8,200 crore, beating analyst estimates of around Rs 7,096 crore by a wide margin
  • Margins continued to expand, building on the company's FY26 EBITDA margin of 33.6% at the full-year level
  • Management has guided for FY27 EBITDA margins of approximately 25%, a step-down from FY26 due to competition on key products

Strong Quarter Despite Headwinds

Lupin Limited reported a strong first quarter for fiscal year 2027 on Wednesday, with consolidated net profit rising approximately 16% year-on-year to Rs 1,415 crore, according to the company's filing. Revenue from operations topped Rs 8,200 crore, significantly exceeding analyst estimates that had pegged quarterly revenue at around Rs 7,096 crore.

The results extend a run of strong performance for India's fifth-largest pharmaceutical company by revenue. In fiscal 2026, Lupin reported full-year net profit of Rs 5,333 crore — a 62.5% jump over the prior year — on revenue of Rs 27,488 crore.

U.S. Business Drives Growth

Lupin's U.S. business has been the primary growth engine, driven by high-value complex generic launches including generic versions of Tolvaptan (branded as Jynarque) and Mirabegron (Myrbetriq). The U.S. segment generated Rs 3,113 crore in the most recent quarter of FY26 for which a regional breakdown is available, growing 47% year-on-year.

The company has guided for billion-dollar-plus U.S. sales in FY27, though analysts expect some erosion as competition intensifies on its top-selling products.

Margin Story: Peak to Moderation

Lupin's EBITDA margins have undergone a remarkable transformation, rising from 10% in FY23 to 29.7% in FY26 — one of the sharpest margin expansions in the Indian pharmaceutical sector. The company has guided for FY27 EBITDA margins of approximately 25%, reflecting anticipated headwinds.

Three factors are expected to compress margins this fiscal year: Tolvaptan faces patent expiry in September 2026, opening the door to additional generic competition; a third competitor for Mirabegron has settled with the brand owner Astellas but has not yet entered the market; and R&D spending is expected to rise to around 8% of sales.

Analysts at Equirus Securities have noted that generic Jynarque, generic Myrbetriq, and generic Spiriva together contribute more than 50% of U.S. revenue and are entering what they describe as a "sharp erosion phase."

Beyond the U.S.

India, Lupin's second-largest market, delivered steady single-digit growth through FY26. The emerging markets segment has shown more volatility but contributed meaningfully in recent quarters, with 45% year-on-year growth in Q2 FY26.

The company's API (active pharmaceutical ingredient) segment has been a relative weak spot, contracting on a year-on-year basis through most of FY26. Management has indicated that the focus remains on higher-margin formulations rather than bulk API sales.

Investment Outlook

Lupin shares have performed well over the past year, driven by the margin expansion story and strong U.S. launches. Analysts covering the stock have a consensus price target of Rs 1,835, though estimates range widely from Rs 1,284 to Rs 2,399, reflecting uncertainty about the pace of product-level erosion.

The key question for investors is whether Lupin can offset the inevitable decline in revenue from its current blockbuster products with new launches. The company's pipeline in inhalation, injectables, biosimilars, and complex generics will be critical to sustaining growth beyond FY27.

What to Watch

The management's earnings call, expected later this week, will be closely monitored for commentary on the competitive landscape for Tolvaptan and Mirabegron, the pace of new product approvals from the U.S. FDA, and any updates on the company's biosimilar pipeline — an area where several Indian pharma companies are making significant bets.
